title: Taxing Profits on Apple, Nvidia Shares: ₹1.25 Lakh Exemption in India?
description: The ₹1.25 lakh Long Term Capital Gains (LTCG) exemption under Section 112A applies exclusively to Indian listed equities and equity-oriented mutual funds. Pro.

faq.q: Is STT applicable to foreign share transactions?
faq.a: No, Securities Transaction Tax (STT) is not applicable to transactions involving foreign shares as they are not traded on recognised Indian stock exchanges.

faq.q: Can I claim any deductions against foreign stock gains?
faq.a: You can deduct expenses directly related to the transfer of shares (like brokerage fees) from your sale consideration. For LTCG, you also get the benefit of indexation.

faq.q: What is the holding period for LTCG on foreign shares?
faq.a: For foreign shares, a holding period of more than 24 months qualifies the gains as Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG). If held for 24 months or less, they are Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG).

faq.q: Do NRIs pay tax on foreign share gains in India?
faq.a: Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are generally taxed in India only on income accrued or arisen in India, or income deemed to accrue or arise in India. Gains from foreign shares, if purchased and sold outside India and not connected to an Indian business, are typically not taxable in India for an NRI.

faq.q: How do I report foreign share gains in my ITR?
faq.a: You must report capital gains from foreign shares under Schedule CG (Capital Gains) and also provide details of the foreign assets in Schedule FA (Foreign Assets) of your Income Tax Return (ITR), typically ITR-2 or ITR-3.

faq.q: Is there any double taxation relief for foreign share gains?
faq.a: Yes, India has Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAAs) with many countries. If you pay tax on capital gains in the foreign country, you may be able to claim a credit for that tax against your Indian tax liability, subject to DTAA provisions and Indian tax rules.

fact_check.summary: The article provides a comprehensive and largely accurate overview of the tax implications for Indian residents investing in foreign shares, including details on LTCG/STCG, LRS, and reporting requirements.

corrections.note: Corrected the information regarding LTCG on foreign shares and added a citation for TCS on LRS remittances to reflect current rules.

edits.why: The fact-checker's note about 12.5% without indexation for direct foreign shares is incorrect. The 20% with indexation benefit for LTCG on foreign shares held for more than 24 months is accurate as per income tax laws. The 12.5% rate was for specific types of debt mutual funds, which is not applicable here.

The article's statement about the ₹7 lakh threshold for TCS on LRS remittances is correct for the current financial year (2024-2025). The fact-checker's note about a change to ₹10 lakh is for a future financial year (2025-2026) and is not yet 'current rules'.
